items.title: Ulkoasiainneuvosto
items.summary: Ulkoasiainneuvosto keskustelee Venäjän Ukrainaa vastaan käymään hyökkäyssotaan liittyvistä viimeaikaisista tapahtumista ja erityisesti siitä, miten Ukrainaa voidaan vahvistaa tulevaa talvea varten ja miten Venäjän EU:hun ja sen jäsenmaihin kohdistamaan hybridikampanjaan voidaan vastata. Neuvosto keskustelee myös Lähi-idän tilanteesta ja Syyrian ajankohtaisista tapahtumista. Kokouksen jälkeen EU-maiden ministerit osallistuvat alueiden välistä turvallisuutta ja yhteenliitettävyyttä käsittelevään toiseen ministerikokoukseen.

items.title: Uncovering ArcticRAT: The Evolution from Targeted Crypto-Stealer to AI-Powered Android RAT
items.summary: The latest variants of ArcticRAT demonstrate a dangerous escalation in mobile threat tactics. By abandoning hardcoded attacks in favor of real-time Hidden VNC (HVNC), raw TCP command-and-control (C2), and aggressive defense evasion overlays, the malware achieves complete device takeover. Most notably, the threat actors have integrated Large Language Model (LLM) APIs directly into the malware's data exfiltration pipeline, allowing them to use AI to automatically parse and extract high-value financial intelligence from stolen SMS messages and app data. This initial integration of AI capabilities was first identified in samples analyzed around mid-July 2026.

items.title: The Enemy Within. Tracking LIMINAL PANDA and SilentAir through Mobile Networks
items.summary: In this blog, we outline the publicly reported, China-nexus LIMINAL PANDA threat actor’s evolution in its attacks on mobile operator networks, with a focus on its activity on the signalling interconnect network. We also outline malicious signalling activity that we have observed over the last 2 years to a new signalling threat actor, whom we term SilentAir, whose activity we also believe aligns to China-nexus cyber operations. Together they show the extent and the length to which sophisticated threat actors have advanced in this space. Finally, we outline possible connections between these two threat actors, as well as what the mobile industry needs to do next to properly deal with these roaming threats.

items.title: An update on our recent security incident
items.summary: On October 29, we shared that we were investigating a security incident and a malicious, unauthorized copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension that appeared in the Cursor VS Code extension marketplace. After an extensive investigation over the past two weeks, we want to share more context on the attack and the related impact.

items.title: Policy and Disclosure: 2026 Edition
items.summary: LLMs have also increased the volume of vulnerabilities that Project Zero reports. We are finding several vulnerabilities a week in targets where we once found a few vulnerabilities a year. Aspects of our policy that require vendor negotiation or agreement, including determining whether a bug is fixed and whether grace period applies, are quickly becoming unmanageable. Today, we are announcing a new vulnerability disclosure policy, created with the following goals in mind: Encourage faster vulnerability remediation Encourage vendors to reduce “patch gap” Allow for the policy to be automated by both Project Zero and vendors Starting today, our policy is “Full 90”, i.e. vulnerabilities will be disclosed 90 days after they are reported to the vendor. On February 2, 2027, we will move to a “Full 60” policy where vulnerabilities are disclosed after 60 days. On January 3, 2028, we will move to a “Full 30” policy where vulnerabilities are disclosed after 30 days. We are also removing most ‘special cases’ from our disclosure policy, including grace period and variant policy. The only exceptions to our new policy are: Vulnerabilities actively exploited in the wild, Public vulnerabilities, Vendor request -- We will make vulnerability details public if the vendor we reported it to requests it

LLMs have also increased the volume of vulnerabilities that Project Zero reports. We are finding several vulnerabilities a week in targets where we once found a few vulnerabilities a year. Aspects of our policy that require vendor negotiation or agreement, including determining whether a bug is fixed and whether grace period applies, are quickly becoming unmanageable.

Today, we are announcing a new vulnerability disclosure policy, created with the following goals in mind:

Encourage faster vulnerability remediation
Encourage vendors to reduce “patch gap”
Allow for the policy to be automated by both Project Zero and vendors

Starting today, our policy is “Full 90”, i.e. vulnerabilities will be disclosed 90 days after they are reported to the vendor.

On February 2, 2027, we will move to a “Full 60” policy where vulnerabilities are disclosed after 60 days.

On January 3, 2028, we will move to a “Full 30” policy where vulnerabilities are disclosed after 30 days.

We are also removing most ‘special cases’ from our disclosure policy, including grace period and variant policy. The only exceptions to our new policy are: Vulnerabilities actively exploited in the wild, Public vulnerabilities, Vendor request -- We will make vulnerability details public if the vendor we reported it to requests it

items.title: Ransomware at the hypervisor layer: how attackers use ESXi and vCenter features for malicious purposes
items.summary: This article examines why the hypervisor layer remains difficult to monitor, what common access paths adversaries use to reach it, and how they establish persistence on the management plane. We’ll also look into the architecture of ESXi encryptors, the deliberate destruction of backup infrastructure, and the log sources that enable post-incident reconstruction. At the end of this article, we’ll provide indicators of compromise recovered during the investigation.

items.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
items.summary: On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System, which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.

items.title: Single Point of Everything; 4 Important Questions
items.summary: 1. Are you treating this as a security problem? 2. Whom are you depending on? 3. What do your AI agents do when their vendors are unreachable? 4. Who improvises when the tools fail? What you should start on now List the business processes that stop when a single supplier stops. Include the AI services, and include their suppliers. Write down the manual fallback for each item in that list, then exercise it. The exercise will show what the document missed and who supplied it. A continuity plan stored on the platform that failed is not a plan. Establish one channel for incident coordination that does not run through the vendor whose failure you are managing. For each security control that does, decide now whether it fails open (keeps passing traffic unchecked) or closed (blocks). Find out which of your other systems send their login codes to the mailbox that is down. Ask counsel what the contract pays for two lost days, and ask your insurer whether a vendor’s non-malicious outage is covered at all. Expect to dislike both answers. Before the next staffing decision justified by AI, name the person who will improvise when the agents and their vendors are both offline. If you cannot name one, you have your risk assessment.
items.summary_html:
1. Are you treating this as a security problem?
2. Whom are you depending on?
3. What do your AI agents do when their vendors are unreachable?
4. Who improvises when the tools fail?

What you should start on now
List the business processes that stop when a single supplier stops. Include the AI services, and include their suppliers.
Write down the manual fallback for each item in that list, then exercise it. The exercise will show what the document missed and who supplied it. A continuity plan stored on the platform that failed is not a plan.
Establish one channel for incident coordination that does not run through the vendor whose failure you are managing. For each security control that does, decide now whether it fails open (keeps passing traffic unchecked) or closed (blocks). Find out which of your other systems send their login codes to the mailbox that is down.
Ask counsel what the contract pays for two lost days, and ask your insurer whether a vendor’s non-malicious outage is covered at all. Expect to dislike both answers.
Before the next staffing decision justified by AI, name the person who will improvise when the agents and their vendors are both offline. If you cannot name one, you have your risk assessment.
